summary: Module 3 CONTEXT micro-exercise applied to the REAL fork task 'Add a POST /teams endpoint'. I sorted the actual fork files into the Context Triangle buckets instead of a hypothetical project. ARCHITECTURAL (how we do things here): app/routers/links.py (existing endpoint patterns: status codes, response_model, Depends wiring, error_envelope via HTTPException), app/errors.py (error_envelope format + redact), app/main.py (middleware + exception handlers + router registration), app/config.py (Settings pattern, env-driven). LOCAL (directly relevant): app/models.py (Team/TeamMember/Invitation -- the data this endpoint touches), app/deps.py (get_current_user -- the auth dependency to reuse), app/schemas/team.py (the request/response DTOs already drafted), app/services/teams_service.py (create_team business logic), migrations/migrate.py (how tables are created). CONSTRAINT (must NOT do): requirements.txt (do not add dependencies -- pydantic/FastAPI/SQLAlchemy already present), app/database.py (must use get_db/get_db SessionLocal, never create a new engine), the interface contract from M2 (roles admin|member|viewer, owner = teams.created_by, TeamResponse.owner_id is presentational mapped from created_by), error format rule (always raise HTTPException so main.py's handler wraps in error_envelope -- never return raw dicts for errors). NOISE (leave out of the briefcase): README.md, .env.example, CI config (railway.json/.github), migrations for users (unrelated schema), tests/test_links_service.py for THIS endpoint write task (helpful only if writing tests), app/worker/* (celery, unrelated to teams), test_analytics etc. Context-triangle lesson internalized: essential = files that define pattern+constraints+integration for THIS task; helpful = testing patterns + dependency list; noise = anything about importance-in-general rather than relevance-to-task. The key distinction the module stresses: these are not the most important files in the project -- they are the most important files FOR THIS TASK. The POST /teams case shows all three failure modes: omit architectural -> agent invents error format; omit local -> agent guesses import paths / file names; omit constraint -> agent installs a new validation lib or auth check. My M2 experience confirms: the Task 2 prompt lacked the local context (actual schema) and the agent silently invented its own resolution -- exactly the 'guesses at file names and signatures' failure.
evidence: Actual fork files sorted into architectural/local/constraint/noise for POST /teams
All three triangle failure modes mapped to concrete fork consequences
M2 BREAK cited as live example of omitted local context causing agent divergence
